Title: SN->SR->LLR->TC join + orphan set
Detail: Loads the four registries, computes the orphan set (SR without LLR/TC, LLR/TC without a parent, SN without an SR), and exits 1 under --strict.

Title: Id + CSV-structure + citation integrity
Detail: Duplicate/malformed id detection per ID_PATTERNS, a per-row column-count check, and SR/LLR citation coherence (triangle_findings); the always-valid --strict-integrity floor.
Rationale: These three are wrong the moment they are written rather than at a gate, and each corrupts the join before the orphan rules could notice — so they run on every commit rather than waiting for a gate that would inherit an already-broken registry.

Title: Placeholder + schema checks
Detail: -000 example-row scan and required-field + closed-vocabulary validation over the real (non-placeholder) rows, plus the ratified-phase completeness rule: once any spine row is phased, a non-Draft SR/LLR/TC whose Phase does not digit-parse to a number is a --strict-schema finding (vacuous until armed; a downstream vN parses and passes).

Title: Comparative-term advisory
Detail: Flags an AcceptanceCriteria comparative term with no predicate marker in the cell; warn-only, never joins the failure set.

Title: Off-spine integrity + back-links
Detail: Integrity-checks the PB/REPO/PART/ASSET ids plus legacy MOD compatibility and resolves REPO/MOD DelegatedSRs against the SR set; -000 example rows ignored.

Title: Gate step plan + missing-tool guard
Detail: Builds the required-step plan per gate/tier and reports SKIP(missing) with a nonzero exit when a required tool is absent. On a claimed work branch (_work_branch: current git branch with a docs/work/active/<branch>/ directory; memoized, fail-closed to full checks off-git or on '..' names) the _TRUNK_FRESHNESS_STEPS set SKIPs with a §5.2 notice, exit code untouched; the plan listing still names every step.

Title: Stack profile loader
Detail: Reads format/lint/test/tiers/coverage/arch-map from docs/stack.ini and resolves each step's command from that profile.

Title: Profile validation
Detail: Rejects a malformed profile, non-integer coverage threshold, or missing declared binary with a clear loud failure.

Title: Conditional profile seeding
Detail: Selects the file/skill set per stack+domain scope; omits Python-only artifacts and seeds files-mode arch-map for a non-Python stack.

Title: Scaffold writer
Detail: Writes the mapped kit files into --dest so the generated harness runs green out of the box.

Title: Idempotent write + kit-version stamp
Detail: Skips an existing file unless --force.

Title: Link + vision-tag checker
Detail: Resolves intra-repo links, requires a PROJECT-VISION tag, and checks generated-doc freshness under --stale.

Title: Flow-doc contract checker
Detail: Validates an authored runtime-flow doc against its structural contract; a malformed flow fails.

Title: Budget comparator

Title: PB back-link resolution

Title: Stub marker detector

Title: Secrets pattern scan

Title: Two-axis privacy gating

Title: Pre-commit floor
Detail: Runs trace --strict-integrity and the check_privacy secrets scan on staged content and blocks a failing commit.

Title: Pre-push outgoing scan
Detail: Scans the outgoing commit range and blocks a push that would publish a secret or a private identity under privacy-check.

Title: Hook python probe
Detail: Probes candidate interpreters by running one and skip-or-reports clearly when none works or a Store-alias exits nonzero.

Title: Vendored-doc drift check
Detail: Compares a vendored doc copy against its recorded upstream source and reports drift.

Title: Arch-map splice + drift check
Detail: Regenerates the symbol map inside the BEGIN/END marker block and fails --check when the committed map has drifted.

Title: Permutation expander
Detail: Parses the Permutations grammar (range/set/bool with @full|@pairwise|@boundaries) and emits the concrete case set.

Title: Skills index generator
Detail: Reads each SKILL.md applicability frontmatter and regenerates skills/INDEX.csv.

Title: Headless session launch
Detail: Runs the agent CLI headless: build_argv substitutes {model} into argv and, when a CmdTemplate carries no {prompt} placeholder (the default for both provider CLIs), routes the prompt to the child's STDIN (run_session writes it from a daemon thread then closes), while the no-wedge invariant holds — a fixed prompt plus EOF, never an interactive read. A codex session additionally captures that CLI's own --output-last-message file as the result (_codex_lastmsg_setup/_codex_lastmsg_read). stdin is otherwise closed so no prompt wedges the loop; the scope is the dispatcher and worker sessions, and the former status.md-resume read is retired rather than coexisting with them.
Rationale: A large prompt passed as argv dies at the OS command-line cap (8191 characters through a Windows .CMD shim, 32767 via CreateProcess) and a round's briefs run to roughly 70k, so stdin is the only delivery that survives — both limits verified live rather than assumed. The last-message capture exists because that CLI echoes its banner and the whole prompt into stdout, so stdout is not the result.

Title: Preflight footing guard
Detail: Refuses a non-git dir, a missing agent CLI, or a private author under privacy-check with a typed nonzero exit rather than hanging.

Title: Typed outcome + ERROR handling
Detail: Ends each session in a typed code, guards a zero-commit HEAD, and reports an all-ERROR region as an unavailable agent, not a work stall.

Title: Kernel advisory lock
Detail: Takes an OS advisory lock the kernel releases on process death, so no stale-pid file wedges the next run.

Title: Lock mutual exclusion
Detail: Refuses a second coordinator holding the same per-worktree lock, preventing a two-writer race.

Title: Shared declared-line parse
Detail: The single first-non-comment-line reader the hooks, agent_loop.read_declared, and check_privacy all use so a declared policy value is read one way.

Title: Onboard/dev-setup templates
Detail: The onboarding and dev-setup scaffold scripts that materialize and run to a green developer setup.

Title: Release checklist generator
Detail: Emits docs/release-checklist.md, including a Performance-budgets section listing each warn-tier PB (id + allocation) read from the budgets registry.

Title: WI dependency-DAG validation
Detail: Loads the WI registry - the docs/work/ spec folder, or a legacy work-items.csv via dual-read (folder wins when it holds real specs; both-present is an integrity error) -; validates WI ids, predecessor resolution, and hard-edge acyclicity; respects the absent/placeholder/opt-out vacuity rules.

Title: Offline project-state core
Detail: Renders one self-contained root HTML file with completeness tiles, the spine hierarchy, and the WI roadmap DAG.

Title: Duplicate-block detector
Detail: Tokenizes each source file (stdlib tokenize; comments/NL/indent excluded, NEWLINE kept so windows cannot stitch unrelated statements), slides a --min-tokens window (default 30), groups candidate hits by line offset, and merges only step-1-overlapping token-window offsets into one finding per block, POSIX-normalizes the file pair, and fingerprints each block (a hash of its complete token signature, line-number-free). A finding is suppressed only when its fingerprint+pair is recorded in docs/dupes-allow (count-aware: N lines sanction N identical copies) or a legacy bare pair matches; --emit-census prints the lines.

Title: Per-phase cmd map + size tripwire
Detail: cmd_map parsed by parse_map (same KEY=value syntax; templates may not contain , or ; — the dispatcher wrapper covers those); session_template(phase) falls back to AGENT_CMD; every map entry preflighted (parse + executable); review-policy read via read_declared and printed in the banner; status_size_warning is pure and warn-only (limit<=0 disables).

Title: Path + sym: reference checker
Detail: Scans root *.md + docs/**/*.md; a backticked token is path-shaped when it carries a separator plus a known extension or top-level prefix (URLs/globs/placeholders excluded); GENERATED marker blocks and path-ok lines are skipped; sym:<module>.<name> is resolved against the module map parsed from architecture.md (module tail -> public symbols); warn-first, --strict exits 1.

Title: OKF bundle emitter
Detail: emit() builds {relpath: content} for every real row (sorted, deterministic, no timestamps): frontmatter via JSON-quoted YAML scalars, bodies carrying the row prose plus up/down markdown links from locally built reverse maps, per-tier and root indexes, the UPSTREAM.md spec pin; on_disk() snapshots docs/okf for the byte-compare; write mode writes-if-changed and prunes; small loaders duplicated per the F5 rule (no new sibling import). Layer B2 adds a process-guides tier: _doc_title_and_summary derives each guide title+summary from the doc first heading/paragraph (inline links stripped so nothing dangles), emitted only after the vacuity gate so a fresh scaffold stays vacuous.

Title: Subagent spawn gate
Detail: Pure decide(tool_name, policy, override) -> allow|ask|deny|defer over SPAWN_TOOLS={Task,Agent}; main reads the PreToolUse JSON payload, reads docs/subagent-gate via the shared declared-line parse, applies the SUBAGENT_GATE=allow override, emits permissionDecision (deny -> exit 2), and appends each decision to docs/subagent-gate.log; any exception fails OPEN (allow) and logs, so a broken gate never wedges the agent's tools.

Title: IF-tier integrity
Detail: Loads interfaces.csv; validates IF ids, SR back-links and Component tags, and emits the best-effort endpoint-module advisory.

Title: Architecture-connectivity coverage warns
Detail: Emits opt-out warn-first findings for missing endpoints/directions, uncited Active seams, and dangling Contracts citations without changing exit status.

Title: Cross-agent skill fan-out drift check
Detail: gen_skills_index.check_agent_sync byte-compares each per-agent <agent>/skills/<name>/ file (.claude/.gemini/.agents) to the neutral project-trajectory/skills/<name>/ source; a copy that diverges is a --check-agents finding with a one-command fix, an orphan copy (no source) a non-failing warn, a source skill missing from a subset dir no finding. Vacuous without a source or per-agent dir; wired as the check.py skills-sync step + pre-commit floor (kit-only generator, so a scaffold no-ops). bootstrap.sync_agent_skills (--sync) force-refreshes only the <agent>/skills/<name>/ subtree from source.

Title: Agent pair-row routing
Detail: Parses pair rows and enable tokens; resolves versions; merges Env; selects by tier, family, cooldown, and order with legacy Provider compatibility.

Title: Managed review dispatch
Detail: Schedules review-policy sessions in managed mode, constructs redacted prompt-map briefs, parses verdicts, logs selections, and preserves unmanaged behavior.

Title: Review substance scorer
Detail: Computes advisory substance components and decay history; treats tripwires as gates and never rewards length.

Title: Run capability menu reader
Detail: load_capabilities parses the docs/stack.ini [run] section (configparser, interpolation=None, case-preserving optionxform; declaration order kept; a name.desc row attaches to its command and an orphan or empty-value command is dropped) into an ordered (name, command, desc) list; --list prints name<TAB>desc per row; direct(name) launches by exact-match name (exit 2 on an unknown name) and launch() runs the shell line via subprocess shell=True, passing the child exit code straight through; interactive_menu prints the numbered menu, reads a pick from stdin, and returns EOF-safe without hanging; an absent or empty [run] prints guidance and exits 1. The run.* launchers are thin delegates forwarding their args to run_menu.py.
Rationale: The command being run is the user's own declared line, so shell=True is the same trust boundary the declaration already establishes rather than a new one. EOF-safety is load-bearing: a menu that blocks on a closed stdin turns an unattended invocation into a hang, which is the failure this launcher exists to avoid.

Title: Independent critique dispatch
Detail: Detects Critique-scoped builds and assembles a fresh family-heterogeneous rubric/intent/artifact brief with no self-assessment.

Title: Bounded software top view
Detail: Derives component roots and uncontained modules; enforces TOP_VIEW_MAX with nesting, opt-out, and vacuity rules.

Title: Derived-gate computation + hybrid cache
Detail: Per-artifact gate rules (sr_gate/maturity_gate/sn_gate) + min-aggregation over in-scope artifacts + the cached docs/gate (basis line + --check rot guard, legacy value-only); the derived current phase (max over ratified rows via phase_num) rides the basis line and --print, the phase analogue of the derived gate. is_modified is recognized (F5-mirrored from trace.py, pinned by test_rule_sync) and counted across SR/LLR/TC onto the compared basis line as modified=N beside drafts=N - a surfacing count only, no gate arithmetic (a Modified SR reads G2 through the existing decomposed-unverified rung of sr_gate; maturity_gate stays Draft-only so a Modified child never caps).

Title: Process reference tab
Detail: Renders the Process tab as a fully self-contained conditional panel registered in build_html (the Knowledge-tab pattern: nav button + section id=process): (1) the artifact-lifecycle x gates panel derived from the live registries + docs/gate (current-gate highlight; per-tier counts from the spine), (2) the resume-loop panel (the managed agent_loop flow with its escalation edges), (3) the slices -> phase -> gates panel derived from the WI registry (docs/work/); links out to the process masters wherever a canonical home exists (bounded in-view restatement only where no single doc states the relationship); sorted inputs, no clocks; a data-less repo renders byte-identically; --check unchanged (the trajectory-map step).

Title: Tiered When roadmap
Detail: Builds phase/workstream/WI tiers by threshold, surfaces delivery Phase, and aggregates parent edges from deduplicated child edges.

Title: Dashboard usability rendering
Detail: Adjudicated against the usability rubric (docs/rubrics/dashboard-usability.md) by the SR-084/SR-085 critique loop: labels stay readable at default zoom with no clipped or overlapping text, and the reading experience the rubric's remaining anchors describe. Byte-deterministic; --check unchanged. This row keeps ONLY what a test cannot pin: the mechanized cores have left for child rows that name the tests owning them — T2 start-collapse (LLR-099/TC-102), T3 breadcrumb-restores-parent (LLR-100/TC-103, the whole anchor, no residue here) and T1 labelled entry (LLR-115/TC-120, the whole anchor, no residue here). Do NOT restate a child's claim here: an anchor lives in exactly one row.
Rationale: A critique that re-judges what a test already enforces spends its budget twice and can disagree with the harness, so an anchor whose bar becomes operational leaves this row entirely rather than being kept as a duplicate. T3 and T1 are the two that left whole: a critique cannot verify T3's return path from a static shot set while a test can click the crumb, and T1's 'obvious' was always glossed as labelled-not-unlabelled, which is mechanizable once written that way.

Title: Process tab intake + human-decision loop panels
Detail: Extends SR-050's process_panel with the project's two circular working loops as linked flow panels: (A) the intake loop - owner/agent intake -> triage into work items with spec detail -> the scheduler-derived ready frontier in the WI registry (docs/work/) -> build/review -> merge; (B) the human-decision loop - open-items population (incl. the gate-ratification table) -> human review and ruling -> the log's Decisions record -> merge - with the LLM_Agent entry node rendered once and shared by both loops. Each stage links to its canonical home (status.md, the WI registry (docs/work/), open-items.html, log.md); data-derived where a canonical source exists; a data-less repo renders byte-identically; --check unchanged (the trajectory-map step).

Title: Decomposition render polish (columns, arrows, persistent hover)
Detail: Polishes the tiered decomposition render: each tier column is sized no wider than its content within a declared bound (a per-tier max-width cap MAX_TIER_COL, not the current uniform column); one horizontal parent->child arrow is drawn per containment edge so containment is explicit rather than implied by nesting alone; and the hover/focus highlight persists on the last-hovered item until another takes it (a stateful highlight keyed to the last-hovered node id, killing the flash-on-exit). Self-contained, byte-deterministic; --check unchanged. Composes with SR-089's tiering without changing its >3 thresholds.

Title: WI-DAG frontier + deterministic traincar ordering
Detail: Derives the dependency-ready frontier from the WI registry + dispatcher reservations (never prose), excludes blocked/deferred/reserved/protected-/exclusive-conflicting WIs with reason codes, and exposes ready --explain / --format json and simulate --jobs N.

Title: Pure safety classifier
Detail: Maps declared safety and policy inputs to one scheduling class and deterministic reason codes without side effects.

Title: next-wi/run-phase retirement + generated status/run-state
Detail: Deletes docs/next-wi + docs/run-phase and every live dependency across agent_loop/prompts/checks/bootstrap/process/tests; translates no former next-wi content into Priority.

Title: Explicit WI/train/worktree worker assignment
Detail: Replaces internal --track assumptions with explicit --wi/--train/worktree assignment; assembles the worker prompt from AGENTS.md + WI row + SpecRef + predecessor context + train diff + rework finding (never status.md/next-wi); collision-safe per-assignment logs/review evidence naming the exact reviewed commit; the --track lane machinery is retired outright.

Title: Dispatcher + worktree pool + atomic reservations
Detail: agent-resume dispatcher/integrator with --jobs (default 2)/auto/AGENT_JOBS; reconcile->gate->build-out launch; packs the frontier into traincars and dispatches dependency-clear ones to free workers.

Title: Traincar continuation + fork/join + release-on-end
Detail: Continues a lane onto the reserved traincar's single hard successor while conditions hold (classifier permits, cap default 4); a fork integrates the parent then splits, a join starts from the combined HEAD.

Title: Serialized train composition
Detail: Applies and reviews one train through the serialized writer, regenerates authority, runs the combined bar, and CAS-advances integration.

Title: Git evidence enumeration
Detail: Enumerates durable reservations, train commits, integration refs, and publication intents before choosing or initializing authority.

Title: Parallel telemetry + downstream migration/audits
Detail: Reason-coded events aggregated by (train, WI, session) + a lanes/frontier/queue/ceiling banner.

Title: Cross-component import coverage
Detail: Joins imports, component membership, and declared seams; reports uncovered cross-component edges with strict/plain and vacuity rules.

Title: Spec interface-section validation
Detail: Validates armed spec interface ids, Proposed rationale, and the intra-module escape with warn-first/strict severity.

Title: Rival-plan coverage comparison
Detail: Parses rival plan tables; resolves clause/SR/IF coverage; validates dependencies; emits pairwise differences and distinct findings/malformed/absent-registry outcomes.

Title: Typed dual-plan round lifecycle
Detail: Implements typed round steps, spend and action caps, position-swapped agreement, persistence, and PAGE mapping.

Title: Allowlist-only dual-plan briefs
Detail: Builds planner/critic/arbiter briefs only from SR/IF registries with strict template slots and override/fallback loading.

Title: Dual-plan planner pair and fallback
Detail: Selects two fresh planner sessions across families where possible and applies the bounded nonresponse fallback with reason codes.

Title: Coverage-step result adapter
Detail: Converts coverage CLI results and report payload into clean, implicated-repair, repeated-failure, or malformed round records.

Title: Dual-plan artifact persistence and filer
Detail: Allocates stable round/stage artifacts and appends registry-valid selected child WIs with mapped predecessors and preserved line endings.

Title: Generated-status source-of-truth guard
Detail: Finds done WI tokens only in hand-edited status.md, with plain/strict severity, and stands down for the generated marker, open/unknown ids, opt-out, and absent status.

Title: Fresh-session dual-plan runner
Detail: Runs planners, cross-critiques, bounded revisions and position-swapped arbiters as fresh sessions; selects only true-plan agreement.

Title: WI row coherence
Detail: Enforces Deliverable iff done on every run and resolvable open-WI SpecRef under strict mode.

Title: Conditional architecture and knowledge views
Detail: Renders software/component and OKF views only when their source bundles exist; omits each otherwise.

Title: Deterministic responsive dashboard freshness
Detail: Produces deterministic responsive HTML.

Title: Declared-interface graph rendering

Title: Fixed review escalation

Title: Bounded critique rework
Detail: Loops CHANGES-REQUESTED through rework and fresh critique within AGENT_CRITIQUE_MAX, then pages via gate policy.

Title: Critique verification vocabulary
Detail: Accepts Critique as a verification value while retaining the LLR completeness requirement.

Title: Critique closure ratchet
Detail: Warns when a Critique-scoped WI closes after CHANGES-REQUESTED with no TC, test, or rubric delta.

Title: Containerized How-SW rendering
Detail: Renders nested component membership and boundary-aggregated seams, falling back byte-identically to the flat view without containment.

Title: Tiered How-SW hierarchy
Detail: Tiers component containment to modules and bounds the visible top level by TOP_VIEW_MAX.

Title: Hierarchy seam ports

Title: One-layer hierarchy navigation
Detail: Handles pointer and keyboard one-layer descent and breadcrumb restoration in self-contained views.

Title: Structural safety cross-check
Detail: Cross-checks declarations against spine, critique, checkpoint, and dual-plan evidence; quarantines only the contradictory WI.

Title: Safety-aware traincar packing
Detail: Packs ordinary chains, serializes protected work, isolates forced-single work, and batches only homogeneous cap-bounded spine-serial work.

Title: Serialized blocked disposition
Detail: Commits a smaller blocker-only disposition carrying BlockRef/evidence and no review-pass claim.

Title: Durable publication intent
Detail: Persists expected-old and target hashes, CAS-publishes, and syncs only a clean/expected development worktree with recoverable failure evidence.

Title: Ownership-state reconstruction
Detail: Reconstructs one owner/state per WI and train from Git evidence; quarantines ambiguity and duplicate claims.

Title: Lifecycle-boundary recovery
Detail: Recovers each reservation/integration/publication fault boundary without runtime-cache authority or evidence loss.

Title: Dual-plan path isolation
Detail: Rejects dual rows on the direct worker path.

Title: Serialized dual-plan disposition
Detail: Commits SELECT or PAGE as one docs-only disposition and regenerates validation.

Title: Spec-lifecycle close-side findings
Detail: Emits R-F findings - done WI with non-empty SpecRef; live docs/specs file (README/-000 excluded, the spec_interface_findings idiom) with no open-WI citer - message-only, riding main's warn-plain/error-under-strict tier with no new branch.

Title: Per-module coverage-floor comparator
Detail: Reads the docs/coverage-floors census (module + min percent; blank and # lines ignored) and coverage.py's JSON report (per-file percent_covered, path-normalized), fails on any module below its floor or absent from the report, SKIPs when the report is absent, is a no-op with an empty census, and fails loudly on a malformed floor line.

Title: Default-density start-collapse (T2 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of usability anchor T2 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-usability.md): a view whose scale EARNS tiering — a bundle spanning more than 3 OKF types, a module set above the component threshold (the SR-089 '>3' rule) — renders START-COLLAPSED as the shared type-tiered drill, one block per type or container, rather than a flat wall of nodes; at or below the threshold it stays flat. Covers the Knowledge, How-SW and landing What views; the What icicle start-collapses to one block per SN with descend-on-click, reusing _drill_layer_svg/_render_drill so the interaction idiom is single-sourced. SCOPE: T2's remaining 'reads legibly at default density' judgement stays perceptual under LLR-055/TC-055.
Rationale: Tiering imposed on a small project costs a click to reach what already fitted on one screen, so it is earned by scale rather than switched on globally. Capping DEPTH instead of collapsing was rejected and the emitter records why: height is leaf-proportional, so stopping at the SR lane still stacks one unit per SR and the wall returns. The What icicle is the case that forced the widening — it rendered the whole spine at LEAF scale, one unit per test case.

Title: Detail-in-context breadcrumb (T3 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of usability anchor T3 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-usability.md): descending a container never replaces the view with no way back — the drill emits a declared breadcrumb nav (<nav class="crumbs"> with a data-root-crumb root label) whose crumb click TRUNCATES the trail to that ancestor, restoring the parent view. SCOPE: the WHOLE anchor — the breadcrumb's presence AND its restore behaviour; T3 is retired as a critique anchor and no residue is left under LLR-055/TC-055.
Rationale: A drill that descends with no way back strands the reader in a view they cannot leave, and 'keeps the reader oriented' never independently passed or failed a round — the breadcrumb IS that orientation, so the claim becomes testable only once it is the thing asserted. Leaving the anchor to critique was rejected because a critique CANNOT verify it: a shot matrix captures initial views only, so a round can pass on markup while the return path itself stays unverified, whereas TC-103 clicks the crumb. It follows that a critic finding T3 violated has found a gap in TC-103, which routes through change-intake to harden this test rather than through a verdict.

Title: Non-pruning SVG container roles (A2 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of accessibility anchor A2 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-accessibility.md): no emitted <svg> declares the CHILDREN-PRESENTATIONAL role=img over a FOCUSABLE descendant, and any svg that does declare role=img carries its own accessible name (aria-label, or a first-direct-child <title> — per SVG-AAM a <title> nested in a <g> names the <g>, not the svg). Focusable means tabindex in any quoting OR a native SVG <a href>, which is tab-ordered without a tabindex. The role is chosen from the emitted BODY by _svg_role. SCOPE — and no wider: the container-role invariant as PROVEN by TC-104, over the artifact this repo ships plus the tiered fixture plus the predicate's own unit cases; it is NOT a proof over every reachable emitter configuration, so an emitter no rendered artifact exercises is unguarded. Name QUALITY belongs to LLR-108/TC-113.
Rationale: role=img prunes its subtree from the accessibility tree, so declaring it over focusable descendants hides every one of them from assistive technology while the page still looks correct. The predicate must treat a native SVG <a href> as focusable and not tabindex alone: a tabindex-only predicate passes a diagram of linked stage cards that are tab-ordered without one. Setting the role at each call site was rejected — deriving it from the body is what stops a future emitter silently reintroducing the conflict.

Title: One-concept-per-colour de-collision (U5 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of uniformity anchor U5 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-uniformity.md): no hex value is reused across STATUS_FILL/TIER_FILL/OKF_TYPE_FILL/SW_NODE_FILL/PHASE_ACCENTS for an unrelated concept (the intentional TIER_FILL<->OKF_TYPE_FILL SN/SR/LLR/TC mirror is the one exception, asserted as a bijection rather than a set match), no PHASE_ACCENTS entry equals the CSS --accent token, and PHASE_ACCENTS clears a PAIRWISE (not merely adjacent) deltaE floor of 15. SCOPE: hex-identity and deltaE across these five declared palettes; the near-duplicate residue across vocabularies belongs to LLR-109/TC-114.
Rationale: One hex carrying two concepts makes the legend a lie in both directions, and a phase sharing the --accent token makes that phase's focus and hover ring invisible — a control the reader cannot see they have reached. Comparing only ADJACENT entries was rejected: a palette is read as a whole, so two members that collide are a collision wherever they sit in the list.

Title: Uniform node/edge/legend/highlight styling (U3 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of uniformity anchor U3 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-uniformity.md): the hover/focus highlight ring resolves to ONE shared per-fill `--ring` custom property across every SVG emitter (drill/icicle/flat-DAG/knowledge) rather than a different hue per emitter, and the When tab's phase-accent key renders through the SAME `.legend`/`<i>` component every other legend in the document uses rather than a bespoke inline-chip idiom. SCOPE: highlight-token equality and legend-component equality, asserted structurally against the emitted CSS and markup. Spacing and exact visual weight belong to LLR-110/TC-115.
Rationale: A highlight that changes hue between views teaches the reader a different interaction language per tab, and a legend built twice drifts in one copy while the other stays right. Per-emitter hues were the shipped state (an accent token in the drill views, a hardcoded amber elsewhere) and were rejected precisely because nothing held them equal: sharing one token means a change lands everywhere or nowhere.

Title: Process-tab node-label type scale (U1 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of uniformity anchor U1 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-uniformity.md): the Process tab's working-loops SVG no longer hardcodes 12px/9.5px/13px/13px on .stgt/.stgn/.hooplab/.hubname. .stgt/.stgn are the same per-node-label role as the shared --nlabel/--nsub tokens the icicle, dag and knowledge views already share, and reuse them directly; .hooplab/.hubname are a once-per-diagram headline label, a genuinely different role, so they take the one documented --nhead scale step. SCOPE: these four selectors resolve to a declared token, asserted structurally against the emitted CSS. Whether the sizes read as uniform belongs to LLR-111/TC-116.
Rationale: A magic number is invisible to every later change: two independently-drifting literals doing one job diverge the first time somebody adjusts one of them. Collapsing all four selectors onto the node-label tokens was rejected because a once-per-diagram headline is a different role, and forcing one token onto two roles is the same defect in the other direction.

Title: Interactive-control contrast in both themes (T5 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of usability anchor T5 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-usability.md): EVERY control painted over a node's own fill clears the WCAG 3:1 UI-boundary floor against EVERY node fill declared in STATUS_FILL/TIER_FILL/OKF_TYPE_FILL/SW_NODE_FILL/PHASE_ACCENTS, in BOTH themes — computed per fill (white or near-black, whichever contrasts more), never a single fixed hue. Covers the descend/hover/focus ring AND the containment/descend arrow (.cedge shaft plus its marker head), which derives from the same per-fill --ring token; its marker head takes a per-ink marker because marker content is rendered from the defs tree and cannot see the referencing node's custom properties (a constraint recorded in _arrow_markers), and RING_INKS is the closed ink set that makes that emission total. SCOPE: a control's contrast against its host fill, arithmetic like the sibling A4 tests. Whether the affordance otherwise reads as inviting stays perceptual under LLR-055/TC-055.
Rationale: A fixed hue vanishes on whichever fill happens to match it, and the failure is total where it lands: the measured collision put a control at 1.00:1 against its host, i.e. invisible. Fixing only the ring was rejected once the same fixed token was found on the descend ARROW — the very control a reader must find to descend a tier — measuring 1.06:1 light and 1.99:1 dark on a shipped phase fill. One control's fix does not generalise; deriving every such control from the host fill does.

Title: Single-sourced concept colour vocabulary (U2 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of uniformity anchor U2 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-uniformity.md). Every concept's fill is LOOKED UP from a declared module-level palette, so the same concept cannot render two hexes — there is only one place a hex can come from. Concretely: every #rrggbb appearing in a rendered dashboard is either a member of a declared palette collection or a `--token:#hex` theme definition (surfaces, text and borders, which encode no concept). SCOPE: this proves single-sourcing of the VOCABULARY, not that a concept was assigned a well-chosen hue — collision and perceptual separation belong to LLR-102.
Rationale: A vocabulary is one vocabulary only if every member is in it: a bare hex literal outside the declared collection is invisible to the collision sweep and to the ring-ink enumeration alike, so it evades both the checks that would catch it. That is not hypothetical — a four-kind vocabulary declared only three because one badge fill sat inline in its emitter. Auditing hues by review was rejected: review cannot see a member that was never declared.

Title: One interaction idiom per node role (U4 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of uniformity anchor U4 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-uniformity.md). Two node roles exist and each is spelled ONE way in every emitter that renders it: an IDENTIFIED node (icicle .cell, flat-DAG .wi, knowledge .knode) advertises its registry id through `data-id`; a DETAIL-BEARING drill node (.block, in both the When and How-SW drills) advertises its detail-map key through `data-node`; and a node of either role is made focusable the same way, `tabindex="0"` on the group. Neither role ever carries the other's attribute. SCOPE: ATTRIBUTE parity, not runtime behaviour parity.
Rationale: One node addressed two ways means every later consumer must handle both, and the second spelling is the one that gets forgotten. Proving that two emitters' handlers BEHAVE alike was considered and rejected as out of reach without a browser harness — what is provable from the markup is that they are wired through one vocabulary, and that is the narrowing this row accepts explicitly rather than claiming more than it checks.

Title: Accessible-name quality, not merely presence (A2 residue)
CodeSymbol: _render_drill breadcrumb label; every focusable/role=img emit site
Detail: The QUALITY half of accessibility anchor A2, mechanizing what LLR-101 leaves perceptual. Three rules over every focusable element and role=img graphic: it HAS an accessible name; that name is never a bare registry id; and navigation LANDMARKS are distinct. SCOPE, narrower than a first measurement suggests: A2 governs INTERACTIVE elements and meaningful graphics — a <title> on a decorative edge path is a tooltip, not an accessible name. Uniqueness is asserted for landmarks ONLY: a descend control for the same container legitimately recurs across drill layers, one visible at a time, so those repeats are one control reached by different paths. Whether a well-formed, unique, descriptive name is the RIGHT description belongs to SR-054's reading-task critique.
Rationale: A bare registry id tells a screen-reader user nothing about what the control is, and a reader listing landmarks hears a flat list in which two called 'Breadcrumb' are indistinguishable — which is what three drills produce unless the names are made distinct. Asserting over decorative graphics too was rejected: it would manufacture findings the accessibility standard does not make, and a check that cries wolf is one a reader stops reading.

Title: Pairwise deltaE floor across every vocabulary (U5 residue)
Detail: Mechanizes what LLR-102 leaves perceptual: a PAIRWISE deltaE floor across every declared vocabulary, not only within PHASE_ACCENTS. Two floors, each a recorded judgement — 15 WITHIN a vocabulary (every member can sit beside every other in one legend) and 12 ACROSS (two vocabularies share no legend, so the floor is lower rather than absent). The declared tier<->okf mirror is exempt BY DESIGN and is asserted BYTE-EQUAL, so 'exempt' cannot drift into 'nearly equal'. SCOPE: perceptual SEPARATION of the declared palettes. Whether a given hue suits its concept is not asserted.
Rationale: 'A collision the identity check misses' looked like a judgement call only because the formula was already there and nobody had widened the set it ran over — the same arithmetic on more members. A cross-vocabulary floor of zero was rejected on evidence: a reader conflated a pair drawn from two different vocabularies, so sharing no legend reduces the risk without removing it. Three live conflations were sitting in the shipped palettes at the binding — sw external/component at deltaE 8.6, SR/phase[3] at 9.5, Interface/phase[7] at 10.5.

Title: Declared weight/alpha/corner tokens (U3 residue)
Detail: Mechanizes what LLR-103 leaves perceptual. Fourteen CSS tokens plus SVG_RX name one step per role for stroke-width, opacity and corner radius, near-duplicates merged into the role's step, and every emitted value must resolve to a declared token. stroke-opacity is checked under the opacity scale deliberately — it is the same scale applied to a stroke. SVG_RX is enforced against both the source literals and every render, because the rx presentation attribute cannot read a CSS custom property portably. SCOPE: token membership, asserted over paint surfaces (style blocks and style/fill/stroke attributes), never over prose that quotes CSS.
Rationale: 'Spacing and exact visual weight' was undecidable because the weights were never declared: the shipped page carried 8 stroke-widths, 7 opacities, 5 corner radii and 6 SVG rx values, of which five stroke widths were doing the single job 'draw a connector' and four rx values 'round a node box'. Nothing can be uniform against an undeclared scale, so declaring the roles is what turns the judgement into a check; leaving it to review was rejected because a near-duplicate weight is exactly what an eye does not catch.

Title: Declared type scale, no raw font-size literals (U1 residue)
Detail: Mechanizes what LLR-104 left perceptual. 'Do the sizes read as visually uniform' was undecidable because the scale was never written down: 18 raw font-size literals against 5 tokens, with .7/.75rem, .9/.95/.98rem, 1.05/1.1rem and 8.5/9px each being near-duplicate steps for ONE role 3-7% apart. Eleven steps are now declared in THREE documented families - node (px, because SVG geometry is fixed px and a rem resizes labels out of their boxes), page (rem), and one relative step (em, for text sized against its parent) - and every emitted font-size must resolve to one. Claiming a single scale across those units would be false, so the LLR states three. SCOPE: step membership over paint surfaces. Whether the chosen steps are well-proportioned is not asserted.

Title: Keyboard reachability of every wired control (A1 core)
CodeSymbol: emitted querySelectorAll wiring; tabindex + native-link emission
Detail: The mechanized core of accessibility anchor A1 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-accessibility.md): every element the emitted page WIRES an interaction to is keyboard-focusable. The wired set is DERIVED from the document's own DOM-selecting calls and then classified — a control selector (its matches receive per-element click/focus/dblclick/keydown listeners) may match only elements carrying tabindex=0 or natively tab-ordered (a button; an SVG a-with-href, the LLR-101 predicate), and each non-control selector records why its matches are not focus stops. A newly wired selector fails the owning test until classified. The derivation reads EVERY DOM-selecting API (querySelector/querySelectorAll/closest/matches, any quote style) and fails loudly on a non-literal selector argument, which a static read cannot classify. A control-selector wiring loop that attaches click or dblclick must attach focus or keydown beside it, statically asserted. Order-integrity: document order IS emission order, no positive tabindex may reorder the walk, and tabindex=-1 is legal only on the roving tablist buttons. SCOPE — and no wider: focusability, order-integrity and activation PAIRING of the wired set over the shipped artifact plus the seven-fixture emitter sweep. Runtime behaviour equivalence is not driven, and whether the order FEELS sensible stays a reader-experience judgement. Runtime-created controls (the breadcrumb buttons) are native <button>s, keyboard-operable by construction and outside the static walk — a recorded limit.
Rationale: A control reachable only by pointer is unreachable for a keyboard user, and the page still looks complete, so nothing reports it. Enumerating the controls by hand was rejected: a per-element list goes stale the moment a selector is added, whereas deriving the wired set from the document's own calls means a new selector fails until someone classifies it. Two narrowings are load-bearing and must not be relaxed back: the derivation has to read every DOM-selecting API rather than one spelling of one call, or it silently misses wired controls; and the key-handler half has to be asserted statically rather than deferred to a browser, or mouse-only wiring ships.

Title: No information by colour alone (A3 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of accessibility anchor A3: for every declared colour vocabulary (enumerated from the module constants, the U5/U2 closure, so a new vocabulary enters by existing), every member that actually PAINTS in a rendered document resolves to a legend swatch labelled in words in that same document, with CSS tokens resolved. Status members additionally pair a per-status glyph. The emitted JS detail-badge maps are SUBSTITUTED from TIER_FILL/STATUS_FILL rather than hand-copied, and three drift guards hold every copy equal to the constants: the emitted JS maps byte-match the Python palettes; the CSS status tokens match STATUS_FILL and are asserted theme-invariant; and the tier-legend bijection derives its expectation from the TIER_FILL dict, so a member dropped from the legend also fails. SCOPE and its narrowing: the worded cue must exist in the same document — that it sits within eyeshot of the painted element is layout this does not re-assert. The JS detail-panel badge stays out of the LEGEND rule because its background carries its concept as the badge's own visible text.
Rationale: Colour alone excludes any reader who cannot resolve it, and the failure is silent: the page looks informative to everyone who can. A raw hex scan was rejected as the detection method because tokenised fills under-report it — the status legend paints through a CSS variable, and a hex scan finds one member of four. The substitution and the three guards exist because a hand-copied palette copy is the recurring defect here: one stale hex shipped in three separate places, and each copy that a test shares with its emitter is a copy the test cannot catch. The same-document narrowing costs a reader nothing today (every painted member is cued in its own tab panel) and a re-attestation should bless it knowingly.

Title: Text-contrast floors, closed over the vocabulary set (A4)
Detail: Accessibility anchor A4 bound. The WCAG 2.1 AA arithmetic is owned by six sibling tests — node fills vs label ink at 4.5:1, the emitted badge/boundary pairs, the no-opacity-discount rule, theme-token fills behind white text in BOTH themes, the hub-is-not-accent regression, and the per-fill focus ring at the 3:1 boundary floor — so this row adds the BINDING plus the gap none of them owned: the SET. Closed by reflection: every UPPERCASE module-level collection holding hex members must be one of the five declared vocabularies, and every member of the REFLECTED set clears 4.5:1 against its label ink (white, except the one declared queued dark-ink exception) and 3:1 for its computed focus ring. The walk is RECURSIVE (nested dicts, tuples, sets, bare strings), counts any 3/4/6/8-digit hex form as hex-bearing, and requires every member be CANONICAL 6-digit lowercase. The theme-token half is DERIVED from the emitted CSS: every fill:var(--x) token must carry a declared role, white-text-fill roles clear 4.5:1 under white in BOTH themes, container-fill roles keep --text readable in both. SCOPE — and no wider: contrast arithmetic over declared constants and emitted theme tokens (the ring boundary also binds under SR-054 T5 as LLR-105); a lowercase module-level palette would evade the reflection and is forbidden by the module's UPPERCASE-constant convention, a recorded reliance. Rendered-pixel measurement is not asserted.
Rationale: Each sibling test sweeps a hand-copied list of the palettes, so a sixth vocabulary could ship outside every floor check while all six stayed green — the arithmetic was right and the SET was the hole. A new vocabulary must enter the arithmetic by EXISTING rather than by being remembered, which is what reflection buys and a seventh hand-copied list would not. Two shapes of that same defect must not return: a flat-dict-only walk misses nested and non-dict collections, and a hand-listed theme-token set is the very defect this row claims to close — both were live here, which is why the walk is recursive and the token set derived.

Title: Task findability - labelled entry within one tab switch (T1 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of usability anchor T1 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-usability.md). Each of the three core reading tasks the rubric concretizes — find the project state, find the next work, find how the parts connect — is reachable within one tab switch of the landing view, its entry point a LABELLED nav control or a NAMED surface on the landing view, never an unlabelled region a reader must discover by clicking. THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT that makes the check honest: it is judged against the RENDERED artifact carrying real registry data, NEVER the nav skeleton. The guard resolves each task's entry point from the emitted document (task 1 -> the landing Definition-completeness/Execution cards, 0 switches; task 2 -> the landing Next-work card, 0 switches; task 3 -> the How-SW nav tab, 1 switch), asserts each is LABELLED and within one switch, and asserts the next-work surface is NON-EMPTY on the zero-active/all-queued fixture. SCOPE — PROVEN: a labelled entry point per task, reachable in one switch, and the next-work surface non-empty across the practice fixtures (zero-active, waiting-with-predecessor, drained). DELIBERATELY NOT: whether the reader subjectively knows what to do next; T1 leaves the critique entirely, with no residue under LLR-055/TC-055.
Rationale: 'Obvious' was always glossed as labelled-rather-than-unlabelled, and that gloss is the whole bar — once it is written operationally there is nothing perceptual left to adjudicate, so the anchor can leave the critique instead of being re-judged every round. The rendered-artifact constraint is the load-bearing part and must not be relaxed to a structural check: a next-work surface can EXIST in the emitter and render nothing when no row is active, so a nav-skeleton check passes on exactly the artifact a reader finds empty.

Title: Viewport-fit by scale-to-fit with a legibility floor (T7 core)
Detail: The mechanized core of usability anchor T7 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-usability.md). Every emitted SVG (all three wrappers: _svg_wrap for dag/sw/know, the icicle panel, _drill_layer_svg) carries width:100% + max-width:<natural> + min-width:<natural x SHRINK_FLOOR> instead of a FIXED pixel width, so a diagram fills its container and scales down as the viewport narrows. SCOPE and its deliberate narrowing: a view whose natural width exceeds 390 / SHRINK_FLOOR still scrolls horizontally WITH its cue — the row's own fallback rule made mechanical. Closing that remainder needs a narrow-width re-layout (stacked columns), which is not this row.
Rationale: A fixed pixel width pins the rendered size whatever the container does, which is why every narrow view demanded sideways scroll and one graph clipped a component label mid-word. A viewBox alone cannot fix it — the fixed width still wins. The legibility floor exists because pure scale-to-fit TRADES this anchor for T4: a 900px graph squeezed into 390px shrinks a label past readable, so the floor stops the fix from creating the defect it is next to.

Title: Theme-lock: one theme mechanism and no mixed-family surface/ink pair (T6 core)
CodeSymbol: HTML_TEMPLATE theme tokens + every emitter's paint
Detail: The mechanized core of usability anchor T6 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-usability.md). The measurable content is FAMILY PAIRING, not the absence of literals: a fixed status swatch carrying fixed white ink is theme-locked CORRECTLY, since neither side flips. A page inverts mid-view in exactly two ways and this row forbids both. (1) A SECOND THEME MECHANISM below :root — the document declares exactly one prefers-color-scheme block, targeting :root, and one color-scheme, also at :root. (2) A MIXED PAIR — a theme-varying ink on a theme-invariant surface, or the reverse. The two families are DERIVED from the emitted document (the dark block's override set IS the definition of theme-varying), never hand-listed, and the dark block may not override a token :root never declares. Applied to CSS rules declaring both a background and an ink, to every emitted SVG node pairing an inline rect fill with an inline text fill, and to CSS-declared SVG text fills paired against the family their host nodes actually paint in. SCOPE and its deliberate narrowings: --ring is excluded because it is stamped FROM the host fill (LLR-105 owns its floor); the JS-composed badge idiom pairs background and ink at runtime from the invariant vocabulary, where LLR-114's arithmetic owns it; and the page CSS has exactly ONE rule declaring a classifiable background AND ink today (body), so that half is prospective while the sweep's weight sits on the node and text-fill halves. Whether the chosen palettes are PLEASANT stays perceptual.
Rationale: A per-component theme override is a seam the reader crosses while scrolling, and a mixed pair reads correctly in the theme it was authored in and inverts in the other — both are invisible to the author working in one theme. Forbidding colour LITERALS was the obvious rule and is the wrong one: it fails a correct fixed-on-fixed pairing and passes a varying-on-invariant one, so it would flag the safe case and miss the defect. Deriving the families from the emitted document rather than listing them means a new token joins a family by existing.

Title: Generated owner decision surface (registry + attestation depth)
Detail: The RENDERED half of the Modified/Draft attestation regime whose gate SR-049 derives. gen_open_items renders (a) every pending row of docs/requirements/open-items.csv as a decision brief and (b) every SR whose Status is Draft (ratification owed) or Modified (re-attest owed) with its whole chain's per-cell before/after. Two contracts the emitted file carries: the attestation-baseline STAMP (a --since render must be reproducible by the freshness gate, or --check compares against a different history) and the check-the-baseline empty state (an auto-derived baseline sitting AFTER a pre-regime amendment renders no cells, which must never read as nothing-changed). The machine-local advisory region is masked before comparing. SCOPE and its deliberate narrowings: this module RENDERS and owns no second opinion — the attestation model is trace.reattest_model and the pending pointers are gen_trajectory.pending_block, both imported, so a disagreement with `trace.py --ratify` means this view is the defect and the brief wins. NOT claimed: that the rendered page is legible or well-composed.
Rationale: A human cannot bless a delta they cannot see, and the depth that makes a re-attest readable is a WORD-LEVEL diff — which the markdown surface this replaces could not mark, so a reviewer was asked to sign a change they could only read as a whole cell. Re-deriving the attestation model here was rejected: a second opinion that disagreed with the brief would leave the reviewer arbitrating between two surfaces. Both emitted contracts exist because their absence fails SILENTLY in front of someone about to attest, which is the worst place for a quiet failure.

Title: T4 label legibility, mechanized: ink inside its box, truncation with a reveal
Detail: The mechanized floor of usability anchor T4 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-usability.md), widening the anchor's existing owner rather than adding a rubric anchor. The clause made objective: no character a block renders may fall outside that block's own rect, horizontally or vertically. The emitter FITS the sub-label to the column it will actually be drawn in — a second line when one will not hold it, then an ellipsis — with three text lines the ceiling, reusing the grid the id/name wrap idiom already proved fits row_h; a sub-label that already fits one line renders byte-identically to before. SCOPE — PROVEN: for every block of every drill layer in the emitted document, each label line's ink box lies inside its own node rect, measured from the emitted geometry with the emitter's declared per-character widths and the document's declared font sizes, entities counted as the single glyph they render. Second half: this emitter does not truncate the next-work title by a fixed budget — the card emits the whole clause and lets its own width do the fitting, the declared bound _NEXT_WORK_TITLE caps ONE item's HEIGHT rather than its text, and where it bites the remainder discloses through a NATIVE <details> cut at a word so head and remainder rejoin continuously when opened. DELIBERATELY NOT: whether an ellipsis a reader meets is ACTIONABLE — truncated-without-affordance stays T4's perceptual residue under LLR-055/TC-055, so T4 remains a live critique anchor; the full string keeps its homes in the block's title, aria-label and data-summary.
Rationale: A label is illegible AS a label the moment its ink leaves the box it names, which is the half of this anchor a reader cannot argue with. Column right-sizing (LLR-057, SR-056) cannot absorb it: right-sizing clamps at MAX_TIER_COL, so a 400-character need asks for a 2000px column and gets 172 — the overflow is structural, not a tuning problem. A FIXED character budget was the shipped approach on the next-work card and is rejected: it spends the same budget at every width, cutting a title mid-word on a wide screen with the card half empty. Native <details> is the point of the reveal — operable by pointer AND keyboard with no script, in a file opened from disk, which is what makes the affordance assertable from the markup instead of needing a browser. The height bound is measured over 320 registry rows: median 44, p90 126, max 609 characters of leading clause.

Title: No edge through an unrelated node box (T8 objective floor)
Detail: The mechanized floor of usability anchor T8 (docs/rubrics/dashboard-usability.md). T8 is two clauses and this row claims only the first: NO EDGE PASSES THROUGH AN UNRELATED NODE BOX. SCOPE — PROVEN: across the shipped dashboard plus one fixture per emitter, every emitted wire, sampled as the polyline a reader's eye follows, clears every node rect that is not its own source or target. MEASURED at the binding: 264 shipped wires, 0 through a box. DELIBERATELY NOT: crossing count, lane separation, or where a crossing falls — that residue stays under LLR-055/TC-055, which is why T8 remains a live critique anchor. Separately and NOT claimed here: at the router's own 3px clearance rather than the bare box, one wire does graze, so _detour_d exhausting its lane candidates and returning the least-bad fallback is a reachable state rather than a theoretical one; that wire's identity and the lane-separation work belong to the open work item.
Rationale: A wire crossing an unrelated box reads as a connection that is not there, which is a wrong answer rather than an untidy one — geometry a reader cannot argue with. The claim about the ARTIFACT is deliberately separate from the router's own unit tests and is why this row exists: _detour_d returns a LEAST-BAD fallback when no candidate lane clears, so 'the algorithm detours' does not imply 'nothing shipped through a box', and the artifact-level claim had only ever been hand-verified once.

Title: Kit-version stamp
Detail: write_kit_version stamps docs/kit-version (SHA + date, -dirty on an uncommitted kit tree) so a re-sync is diffable.
Rationale: Split from the idempotent-write row: the two obligations share a module but not a failure mode — a scaffold can write correctly and still leave the adopter unable to say what they scaffolded from.

Title: dev-setup wires core.hooksPath
Detail: dev-setup wires the pre-commit floor (core.hooksPath) from its baseline, so the floor is active from the setup the contributor actually runs.
Rationale: Split from the template row: reaching a green setup and being protected by the process floor fail independently, and the second is the one a contributor never notices is missing.

Title: Deterministic traincar ordering
Detail: Orders eligible traincars by (gate, Priority desc, downstream-dependent count desc, hard-path desc, first WI id).
Rationale: Split from the frontier row: deriving WHICH traincars are eligible and deciding WHICH runs first fail independently, and only the second one makes a run replayable.

Title: Generated status + run-state
Detail: Makes status.md an integrator-generated freshness-gated snapshot (never on a worker branch) and run-state a generated RUNNING|NEEDS-HUMAN|BLOCKED|DONE outcome.
Rationale: Split from the retirement row: removing the old pointer and generating the surfaces that replace it are separable, and the second is what keeps the replacement from rotting the same way.

Title: Atomic reservations + worktree leasing
Detail: Reserves constituents atomically via refs/llm/reservations/WI-### (commit-tree metadata + update-ref --stdin zero-old-value); leases worktrees; rescans for dynamic refill; honors pause/blackout/capacity.
Rationale: Split from the launch row: the launch sequence can be correct while the claim is not atomic, and that failure is two workers building the same WI rather than a lane that never starts.

Title: Train build + review shape
Detail: One Build pass (one commit per WI) + one review cycle with the policy-required verdict count; no constituent done until the train integrates.
Rationale: Split from the continuation row: WHEN a lane continues and WHAT shape the resulting train takes are independent, and the second is where the clustering saving is actually realized.

Title: Release unstarted reservations on early end
Detail: Releases unstarted constituent reservations transactionally and recomputes the traincar DAG on any early end.
Rationale: Split from the continuation row: this is the cleanup path, and a cleanup that rides on the happy path's row gets tested only when the happy path is.

Title: Blocked-constituent disposition
Detail: Delivers a blocked constituent's durable disposition through the integrator while independent completed constituents still proceed.
Rationale: Split from the continuation row: a block must outlive the lane that found it, which is a durability property the continuation conditions do not carry.

Title: Gated downstream migration
Detail: Holds --jobs 1 until the soft-edge audit AND the SafetyClass audit pass, then records the two-worker flip; reconciles legacy active rows + docs/tracks/* within one compatibility window.
Rationale: Split from the telemetry row: measuring a parallel run and deciding a repo is ready to start one are different obligations, and only the second can make a repo unsafe.

Title: Dashboard staleness check
Detail: Implements stale/missing --check with a git as-of stamp excluded from stamp-only comparison.
Rationale: Split from the determinism row: determinism is what makes the check possible, but a deterministic artifact nobody re-checks still goes stale.

Title: Contradiction-safe dual-plan class
Detail: Derives contradiction-safe single-WI scheduling from PlanMode and quarantines a contradictory SafetyClass.
Rationale: Split from the path-isolation row: refusing a wrong lane and deriving the right one are separate, and only the second sees a registry contradiction.

Title: PAGE gate-policy mapping
Detail: Applies gate-policy continuation semantics to a PAGE at both the dispatcher disposition and the --dual-plan single-shot round (attended pages, autonomous/single-ratify STALLs).
Rationale: Split from the disposition row: committing the outcome and deciding whether it stops a human are independent, and the second is shared with a second entry point that would otherwise drift.

Title: Spine stand-alone rule
Detail: provenance_findings flags a WI id or a process-doc citation across the normative cells of all three spine registries, joining the --strict failure set via exit_code.
Rationale: A citation is a pointer a later reader may be unable to follow, and the row's reason travels with it: when the work item is closed and archived, the row keeps its claim and loses its justification, which is the failure this catches. Applied to every spine registry rather than the SR alone, because the layer the rule could not originally see held the largest pocket of violations — a narrower scope would guard the cleanest layer and miss the dirtiest.

Title: Requirement form rules
Detail: form_findings applies six rules — one obligation per requirement, no non-obligation modal, no actorless passive, no unfalsifiable term, no open-ended clause, no obligation keyword in an LLR Detail — skipping Draft rows, and joins the --strict failure set via exit_code.
Rationale: A row carrying two obligations reports neither when one fails, and undecidable wording is signed on impression rather than evidence — that is the failure all six rules exist to prevent. Draft is skipped because a Draft row is exempt from the child-completeness rules elsewhere in this harness and is by convention the state a requirement occupies while still being written, so an unfinished acceptance criterion is expected there rather than defective; flagging it would make the state unusable for the drafting it exists to allow. This cell says "obligation keyword" rather than quoting the keyword itself because the rule cannot distinguish a mention from a use, and an exemption a checker cannot see is one an author can reach for.

Title: Paraphrase advisory
Detail: paraphrase_advisories compares a child cell's significant words (alphabetic runs of four characters or more, lowercased) against its parent's and reports when the share of the CHILD's words that also appear in the parent exceeds the declared threshold — the child is the denominator, so a long parent cannot dilute a short echoing child. Reported in its own advisory pipe, which never joins a failure set.
Rationale: A child that re-words its parent adds a second home for one fact and no decomposition, so a later amendment updates one copy and the two disagree with nothing to report it. The advisory has its own pipe rather than sharing the acceptance-criteria counter because a shared count would report 'ac-advisories' about a finding that is not one, and a reader acts on the counter name.

Title: Registry converter (CSV <-> spec folder)
Detail: Converts between the registry homes per the Phase 2a grammar (TOML +++ frontmatter, Deliverable in the body, status from the directory, order key only as a CSV-order migration artifact). --verify round-trips CSV->specs->CSV in a temp dir, exits nonzero on any cell mismatch, and reports byte identity with a reason. write_spec_file is the single spec writer (to_specs and plan_artifacts filing both go through it). Refuses unknown statuses by row and non-empty targets without --force.
Rationale: One writer keeps migration and filing byte-compatible; refusal over catch-all keeps a malformed registry loud rather than silently reclassified.

Title: Serial trunk step (log compile + regen)
Detail: Compiles docs/log.d/*.md into docs/log.md via plan_artifacts.append_log_summary in (git add-time, filename) order - all fragments validated first (name shape, ## heading, reserved section headings refused, committed-in-HEAD required), relative links rebased from docs/log.d/ to docs/, fragments deleted after append, all-or-nothing on any validation error - then regenerates arch-map, okf, derived-gate, dashboard, status block and open-items as subprocesses in dependency order (derived-gate before its two consumers), stopping loudly at the first failure. Never commits; the caller owns the commit.
Rationale: One serial actor per §5.5; derive_gate runs before the dashboard/status regens because docs/gate is their input, not their output.

Title: Tracked pause reader (dual-home)
Detail: tracked_pause parses docs/work/pause as TOML ({reason, since}; absent -> None) and fails closed on malformation with the pinned loud placeholder reason; pause_reason checks the legacy untracked docs/pause first, then the tracked home, preserving the None/''/reason contract so the retired-in-place dispatcher can never resume on a home swap. The legacy half retires with the dispatcher at Phase 5.
Rationale: A broken pause file must still pause; two homes during the migration window, one meaning.

Title: Pause surfaced in the pending block
Detail: Renders zero-or-one 'Paused since <since> - <reason>' bullet in the committed-tree-pure pending region from docs/work/pause - declared since verbatim, no clock, the since clause omitted when empty, fail-closed text on malformation pinned equal to the reader's placeholder.
Rationale: An open pause is a visible accruing cost, never a forgotten one.
